sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Anaphylaxis and Biphasic Phenomena
sections.description: This section establishes the medical foundation required to understand the case, covering the biological mechanisms of anaphylaxis and the distinct clinical definitions of biphasic and multiphasic reactions.
subtopics: Mechanisms of IgE-mediated and non-IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation
Systemic mediators of anaphylaxis: Histamine, leukotrienes, and cytokines
Defining anaphylaxis: Airway, breathing, circulation, and skin manifestations
Biphasic vs. multiphasic anaphylaxis: Definitions, incidence, and timing
The role of systemic mastocytosis in predisposed severe allergic reactions

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Emergency Stabilization
sections.description: This section focuses on the acute presentation of the patient, the diagnostic process in the emergency department, and the immediate life-saving interventions.
subtopics: Initial assessment of an unknown allergen trigger (case focus: clarithromycin)
Clinical signs of anaphylactic shock: Hypotension, hypoxaemia, and urticaria
Immediate management: Rapid administration of epinephrine and supportive care (oxygen, IV fluids)
Assessment of clinical response to initial treatment
The importance of prompt discontinuation of the suspected allergen

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning in Multiphasic and Refractory Courses
sections.description: This section explores the diagnostic challenges faced by clinicians when symptoms recur, focusing on differentiating types of recurrence and using laboratory markers.
subtopics: Differentiating biphasic reactions from refractory anaphylaxis
Evaluating ongoing allergen absorption vs. true biphasic recurrence
Risk stratification for prolonged observation based on severity and response
Laboratory diagnostics: The role of serum tryptase levels in confirming anaphylaxis
Interpretation of tryptase kinetics: Baseline vs. peak and post-resolution samples

sections.description: This section examines the specific treatment decisions made during the multiphasic course, highlighting current controversies and critical dosing considerations.
subtopics: Epinephrine dosing strategies: Weight-based calculations vs. fixed doses
The clinical impact of 0.3 mg vs. 0.5 mg epinephrine auto-injectors in adults
The evolving role of corticosteroids: Evidence for and against in preventing biphasic reactions
Adjunctive therapies: Antihistamines and their role in managing cutaneous symptoms
Management strategies for refractory symptoms: Continuous epinephrine vs. expectant management

sections.section_title: Underlying Predispositions and Long-term Clinical Management
sections.description: The final section looks beyond the acute event to identify underlying conditions and provides a framework for long-term patient education and safety.
subtopics: Clinical indicators of systemic mastocytosis (e.g., hepatomegaly, neuropsychiatric symptoms)
Diagnostic criteria for systemic mastocytosis and the limitations of limited biopsies
Patient education: Training on epinephrine auto-injector use and emergency action plans
Long-term pharmacotherapy for allergic management (e.g., levocetirizine)
The importance of registries for rare complex anaphylactic courses
